# Difference Between Element Sum and Digit Sum of an Array.

@example The true total is 47 + 5 + 120 = 172. The machine adds 4 + 7, then 5, then 1 + 2 + 0, which is 19. 172 - 19 = 153.
[47,5,120]
=> 153

@example Every number has one digit, so the machine gets the total right.
[8,3,6]
=> 0

@example 2000 counts as 2 and 1999 as 1 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 28, for 30 in all; 3999 - 30 = 3969.
[2000,1999]
=> 3969

# The smallest input: one number of one digit.
[1]
=> 0

# The smallest number with two digits: 10 counts as 1.
[10]
=> 9

# The largest value: its three 0 keys add nothing.
[2000]
=> 1998

# Zeros inside a number and at its end must not stop a digit loop early.
[1009,1090]
=> 2079

# Powers of ten up to the four-digit 1000 (a buffer sized for three digits is too small).
[1000,100,10]
=> 1107

# A repeated digit counts every time it is typed: 1111 counts as 4, not 1.
[1111,1999]
=> 3078

# The same number more than once counts each time.
[55,55,55]
=> 135

# One-digit numbers around a large one.
[1,2000,1]
=> 1998

# 17 times 2000: the true total 34000 no longer fits in 16 bits.
[2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000,2000]
=> 33966

# 10 times 1999: the machine's total 280 no longer fits in a byte.
[1999,1999,1999,1999,1999,1999,1999,1999,1999,1999]
=> 19710
